arms.name: LLM Group (ChatGPT)
arms.description: OpenAI ChatGPT was the sole permitted information resource during the initial essay-writing sessions. Participants used a supplied account and could ask for content or revision; other websites and LLMs were prohibited (PDF pp. 23 and 27).

arms.name: Search Engine Group (web search; no LLM)
arms.description: Websites and search were permitted, but ChatGPT and other LLMs were prohibited. Participants used Google; queries included '-ai' to suppress AI-enhanced answers (PDF p. 23).

arms.name: Brain-only Group (no tools)
arms.description: Participants relied on their own knowledge, without websites, online/offline tools or LLMs (PDF pp. 23 and 27).

studies.task: Write a SAT-style argumentative essay on a chosen prompt in each supervised session, with the original assigned tool condition retained across the initial sessions (PDF pp. 25-28).

estimates.notes: Unquantified contrast retained from the screening map; no numerical full-sample effect is reported. The initial-session portions of Figures 47-55 (PDF pp. 76-84) identify assisted and comparison outputs, but show individual/topic-specific scores without printed arm means, SDs, SEs, a full-sample test, confidence interval or standardized treatment effect. No coordinates were read off the figures and no topic results were averaged. Figures 40-46 (PDF pp. 73-76) compare assessors and include pooled displays whose session composition is not established; assessor disagreement is not an AI-assistance effect. The numerical descriptions of selected scores in the topic prose are not full-sample arm means or effects. The arm counts are the reported analyzed original groups in Table 1. A two-arm total and the number of essays/ratings used in these displays are not printed, so n_total and n_units remain null. The original groups remain between-person conditions despite repeated essay sessions; the optional tool-switch subset is excluded.

estimates.notes: Unquantified contrast retained from the screening map. This record is restricted to the initial-session portions of Figures 79-86 (PDF pp. 132-136), which separate sessions and tool groups. The computation is over group/topic pools of essays, not a count of ideas or categories within a person. Higher repetition/overlap means more similar outputs. Neither arm level, an overall difference, SD, SE, confidence interval, test nor standardized effect is printed for a full-sample diversity comparison. The plots and narrative show topic-dependent patterns; no individual phrase frequency, diagram width or topic-specific result is substituted for an overall diversity statistic. Earlier pooled Figures 25-27 (PDF pp. 62-65) do not establish which production phases contribute. The original arm counts come from Table 1; the pairwise participant total and the number of analyzed sets/essays are not printed. The n-gram definitions differ between the early analysis and the session-separated account; this remains an open item.

For initial-session lexical repetition, no scalar full-sample diversity outcome, both arm levels, uncertainty or analyzed set/essay counts are printed (PDF pp. 132-136).

The number randomized, arm-specific randomized counts, timing of exclusions and the rule for omitting a completed case are not stated. PDF p. 22 distinguishes recruited, completed and analyzed counts; Table 1 provides analyzed arm counts only.
Participant-facing ChatGPT model/version and its release year are not reported (PDF pp. 23, 27 and 151). The local Llama model used for judging/NLP must not be treated as the intervention.

Session membership and original-assignment versus current-tool labels remain unresolved for pooled NLP/rating figures, especially Figures 15-21 and 25-46. Same-writer/self-pair inclusion also remains unresolved for Figure 19 (PDF pp. 52-76).

The Figure 21 comparison test, sampling units, exact Cramer's V arm values and treatment of repeated essays/participants are not stated (PDF pp. 58-59). Its labeled p-values do not supply participant-level effect precision.

No full-sample, concurrent after-AI comparison or printed paired uniqueness/diversity estimate is established for the optional returnees. Individual intersession delays are not stated; the study-wide scheduling period is not a follow-up delay (PDF pp. 23, 28 and 117).
N-gram definitions conflict between the early lemmatized analysis and the later session-separated description; Figure 83 and its prose name different repeated phrases (PDF pp. 62, 132 and 134).
Figure 15 leaves the outcome definition and tested null unclear. Figure 16 pooled length means cannot establish a phase-specific effect, and Table 1 describes lengths differently (PDF pp. 4 and 55).

The reference-essay comparison in Figure 18 and its prose does not match the all-pairs expression in equation (1); Figure 12 includes Search Engine transitions despite no Search Engine follow-up (PDF pp. 4 and 52-56).
No participant-linked outcome data or explicit data/code repository is identified in the saved document. The project website on PDF p. 5 is a project link, not an on-file statistical supplement.
notes: Extractor B independently read the complete markdown conversion in consecutive chunks through its end, including references and all appendices, and checked cited pages with PyMuPDF. Table 1 was recovered with find_tables; relevant raster figures were inspected using in-memory PDF renders. No other extractor’s raw file was read. Statistics inventory for eligible original-session outcomes: teacher uniqueness and AI-judge uniqueness are shown in rating/z-score plots (Figures 40-55); no printed full-sample numerical arm levels, treatment effects or uncertainty are available. Initial-session across-writer lexical repetition is described in Figures 79-86 and prose, without a full-sample scalar estimate or uncertainty. The estimate array therefore retains only unquantified records with null statistics; these are not numerical effect estimates. Other potentially relevant statistics occur in Figure 15 (group-labeled length-dispersion p-values), Figure 16 (word/sentence means), Figure 18 (reference-essay cosine-distance means), and Figure 21 (comparison p-values with unlabeled Cramer’s V bars). They are figure-only and/or cannot be assigned to an eligible production phase or construct; their exclusion is documented individually. No number was inferred from figure coordinates, bar heights, degrees of freedom, an approximate narrative proportion or a p-value. PDF p. 22 reports recruitment and completion separately from the analyzed sample; the randomized count is not inferred from any of them. Table 1 supports the original analyzed arm counts. Pairwise participant totals and numbers of essays, ratings, pairs or sets are not calculated. PDF p. 23 explicitly states: "Participants were randomly assigned across the three following groups, balanced with respect to age and gender:". Original assignment is individual, with the same assignment retained during the initial essay sessions. The optional returnees are members of this sample, not new independent arms; no follow-up arm is added to the original counts. No other paper sharing these participants is identified in the screening form or source. The PDF labels itself a preprint. Version identification follows the supplied citation record after confirming the local SHA-256; no API or web lookup was performed. The screening form’s older unresolved version item is thus superseded by the citation record, whereas the outcome/analysis ambiguities remain unresolved. All PDF locators use file page indices plus one; printed page numbers agree at the cited locations. General essay proficiency, physiological activity, memory, self-reports, authorship detection, process measures and selected follow-up/subgroup analyses are excluded under the extraction rules. Only the requested extraction file is written.
